text: . A day after Diwali, a thick blanket of smog engulfed several parts of Delhi this morning, as air quality in the national capital continued to remain in the ‘Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 368 at 7 AM today. The smog also led to a significant reduction in visibility across several parts of the city.The air quality remained poor despite the Supreme Court allowing the bursting of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR during fixed hours on 7th and 8th of November. The court had allowed firecrackers between 6 AM and 7 AM and 8 PM and 10 PM. The Supreme Court further directed that the complete ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR will be restored from today.

. The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) conducted muhurat trading on the occasion of Diwali, marking the beginning of Samvat 2083. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended today’s special trading session in the negative zone. The Sensex ended marginally lower by 29 points to close at 80 thousand 999, while the Nifty dipped 44 points, or 0.18 per cent to settle at 24 thousand 986. Conversely, the broader market on the National Stock Exchange ended with gains. The Midcap 100 index rose over 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index jumped one per cent.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the government is building a modern sports ecosystem through school and grassroots programmes, Khelo India Centres and Olympic-standard training under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS).Felicitating India’s Asian Para Games 2026 contingent for its record haul of 114 medals, Prime Minister urged the athletes to build on their success as they prepare for the Los Angeles 2028 Games.Prime Minister also recalled his appeal from the Red Fort encouraging young people to participate in a nationwide talent hunt with the Olympics in focus. He said Para-sports also receive equal priority under these initiatives.Interacting with the contingent at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi, PM Modi said the performance reflected India’s emergence as a major global sporting power. He congratulated the athletes, their families, coaches and trainers, saying the players had won both medals and the hearts of millions.India secured 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, alongside five world records and nine Asian records. Comparing the achievement with the country’s tally of 14 medals, including one gold, in 2010, PM Modi credited the athletes’ perseverance and dedication.The Prime Minister noted that 34 of the contingent’s 56 female athletes won medals, while Indian competitors swept all three podium positions in four events. The team also won nine gold medals on the final day.Highlighting individual performances, PM Modi said Mona Agarwal set a world record in para shooting, while Haney improved his own world record. He also praised Himanshu, Ravi and Jehan for overcoming physical challenges through their performances.Recalling the sacrifices behind sporting success, PM Modi spoke about Rinku, who lost his mother two months before the Games and held up her photograph after winning gold. “That moment made all of us emotional,” he said.The Prime Minister also highlighted the achievements of younger athletes, noting that 36 of the 61 debutants won medals and Sandeep set a world record on his debut.Describing sports as a means of personality development and nation-building, PM Modi said it teaches discipline, teamwork and the ability to recover from setbacks. He added that the expansion of sports infrastructure, equipment manufacturing and broadcasting was creating employment opportunities beyond the playing field.

. The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha has moved northwards.It is now centred over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said it is likely to move further north and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh tonight.Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.An orange alert has been issued for very heavy rainfall in East Uttar Pradesh, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow. Heavy rainfall is also expected in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.Thunderstorms accompanied by hail are likely over East Rajasthan, Haryana, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand and West Uttar Pradesh.Thunderstorms and gusty winds are also forecast in several other states, including Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam and Meghalaya.Meanwhile Delhi witnessed light to moderate rainfall this evening. The IMD has forecast very light rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning tomorrow morning.The maximum temperature is expected to remain between 26 and 28 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is likely to range from 16 to 18 degrees Celsius.

. National Entrepreneurship Day is being observed today. The day highlights the importance of entrepreneurship in India’s development journey. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was also established on this day in 2014. With over 2.62 lakh Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade-recognised startups, India has emerged as the world’s third largest startup ecosystem, creating employment and expanding opportunities for its youth.Over the past decade, youth have increasingly moved beyond the role of beneficiaries to become active contributors to national development. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship has informed that startups have been able to create more than 23 lakh jobs till March this year. The Government has recognised over 55,200 startups during 2025-26 which is the highest number of startups recognised in a single year since 2016. Along with this, more than 1 lakh recognised startups have at least one woman director or partner.Government initiatives like Startup India, Atal Innovation Mission, Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Startup Hub, Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs (TIDE) 2.0 Scheme, Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups initiative, National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations, Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme and Swavalambini Scheme have supported innovation, easier access to finance, digital platforms, mentorship and enterprise creation. Their expanding contribution reflects India’s growing entrepreneurial capacity and the potential of innovation-led enterprises to support long-term, inclusive development.

. In Men’s Cricket, the second ODI of the five-match series between India and New Zealand will be played in Wellington tomorrow morning. The match will begin at 7:30 AM Indian Standard Time. The visitors will look to extend their lead to 2-0 after registering a five-wicket victory in the rain-affected opening match in Auckland. New Zealand, on the other hand, will aim to bounce back and level the series. New Zealand have suffered a setback as their lead batter Devon Conway ruled out the remaining four matches of the series. Left-handed batter Nick Kelly replaces Conway.

. Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah today inaugurated the newly constructed ISKCON-Sanand Elevated Corridor in Ahmedabad and launched several development projects in Gujarat. In his Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency, Mr. Shah dedicated and laid the foundation stones for 30 projects worth over 1,000 crore rupees. The projects, being undertaken by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, include housing and water supply schemes. The draw for the housing scheme was also completed today.The four-kilometre-long, six-lane ISKCON-Sanand Elevated Corridor has been constructed at a cost of 464 crore rupees by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. It connects ISKCON Junction with the Sanand Flyover, passing through major intersections, including Karnavati Club, Prahladnagar and YMCA.The corridor is expected to ease traffic congestion on the Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway, reduce travel time and ensure safer and smoother connectivity. It is also equipped with noise barriers and advanced traffic management systems to enhance commuter safety and convenience.

. Political leaders from several countries, including French President Emmanuel Macron, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, extended Diwali greetings yesterday, wishing peace, prosperity, unity and hope to people celebrating the festival.In a social media post, Macron extended Diwali greetings to all his friends in India and around the world and wished that the Diwali lights may inspire all to ever uphold unity, peace, and hope. Carney said communities across Canada were joining millions around the world to celebrate Diwali, the Festival of Lights, which marks the triumph of light over darkness, good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. In a social media post, he wished happy Diwali to all who were gathering to light diyas, share meals, and honour traditions passed down through generations.Albanese said Diwali was the great celebration of the victory of light, bringing communities together across religious and cultural boundaries. In a video message on social media, he said, the signs and symbols of Diwali carry a message that speaks beyond religion or culture. It is a call to compassion and understanding, and of love and unity.UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed extended heartfelt wishes to everyone celebrating Diwali in the UAE and around the world. He expressed the hope that this auspicious occasion and the coming year bring excellent health and prosperity to all. Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said Diwali symbolised the triumph of light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance. The true meaning of Deepavali extends beyond illuminating homes with the light of oil lamps. It lies in kindling the light of love, compassion, brotherhood and humanity in the hearts of people, he said.Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also greeted the Hindu community, saying Diwali symbolised the triumph of light over the darkness of hatred, intolerance and despair. Israeli President Isaac Herzog extended greetings to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and people celebrating Diwali in India and around the world. In a social media post, he wished peace, happiness, and prosperity for all on this beautiful festival of lights.Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Diwali should strengthen unity and bridge differences in the country’s diverse society. In a plural society that perpetuates diversity of cultures and traditions, the value of mutual respect, understanding and accepting differences must be continually strengthened, he said.In Thailand, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul inaugurated the Amazing Thailand Grand Diwali Festival 2026 in Bangkok yesterday, in the presence of Indian Ambassador Puneet Agrawal and senior Thai officials. The festival, which will be celebrated for 27 days, is billed as the longest Diwali celebration outside India. It is being organised in collaboration with the Indian Embassy, the Tourism Authority of Thailand, Bangkok authorities and Indian diaspora associations.US President Donald Trump celebrated Diwali at the White House on Friday, lighting a diya in the Oval Office in the presence of Indian-American officials, entrepreneurs and diplomats.

. US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that his administration’s strict immigration policies may have contributed to the Republican Party’s setbacks in the midterm elections.In an interview, Mr. Trump said the deportation drive targeting undocumented immigrants may have been too tough. He noted that while his administration received strong support for securing the US-Mexico border and deporting criminals, its broader enforcement measures had alienated some voters. He acknowledged that the crackdown also affected undocumented immigrants who had established jobs and lived in the United States for several years.The President also expressed willingness to work with Democrats on immigration reforms, as they prepare to take control of both chambers of Congress in January. Meanwhile, the administration’s future immigration policy remains uncertain.

. The Embassy of India in Yemen has successfully evacuated 19 Indian seafarers stranded in Hodeidah and Sana’a for the past two weeks. In a statement posted on social media, the Embassy said all the seafarers are safe, in good health and on their way back to India.It also thanked all concerned for their cooperation in the evacuation operation. In another development, the Saudi-led coalition said its air defence systems intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by Yemen’s Houthi militia towards Riyadh. Residents in parts of Saudi Arabia were also alerted to take shelter amid rising regional tensions.

. In shooting, India’s Niveditha Veloor Nair secured a bronze medal in the women’s 25-metre standard pistol at the ISSF World Championship in Doha, Qatar, yesterday. Niveditha finished third with a score of 567-13x.China’s Xiao Jiaruixuan won gold while Hungary’s Veronika Major claimed silver with. India’s Manvi Jain and Simranpreet Kaur Brar finished eighth and 10th, respectively.In the team event, the Indian trio of Niveditha Nair, Manvi Jain and Simranpreet Kaur Brar secured silver with a combined score of 1,682-33x. With this, India’s overall tally at the Doha championship has risen to seven, comprising one gold, five silver and one bronze.

. The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) conducted muhurat trading on the occasion of Diwali, marking the beginning of Samvat 2083. Benchmark domestic equity indices failed to hold on to their initial gains and ended the day’s special trading session in the negative zone.The Sensex ended marginally lower by 29 points to close at 80 thousand 999, while the Nifty dipped 44 points, or 0.18 per cent to settle at 24 thousand 986. Conversely, the broader market on the National Stock Exchange ended with gains. The Midcap 100 index rose over 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index jumped one per cent.In the Sensex pack, 16 out of 30 companies edged upward. Among the top gainers, SunPharma surged almost three per cent, Tata Steel added 1.9 per cent and Maruti advanced 0.8 per cent. In the top laggards, Mahindra and Mahindra dipped over 0.9 per cent, Indigo dropped 0.9 per cent and Trent fell 0.8 per cent.Among the Sectoral indices at the BSE, 18 out of 28 sectors ended in positive territory. Among the top gainers, Healthcare advanced over 1.6 per cent, Housing Finance rose 1.1 per cent and Industrials added one per cent. In contrast, Realty slipped half a per cent, top 10 banks, Private Banks, and Bankex dropped almost 0.3 per cent, while Consumer Durables lost 0.2 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 3 thousand 253 companies advanced, 947 declined and 254 remained unchanged.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices were trading over 0.3 per cent down in the afternoon session today. The Sensex declined 289 points to 80 thousand 710, while the Nifty fell 81 points to 24 thousand 905, when reports last came in.On the sectoral front, Telecommunication, IT and Cement were the top laggards. Conversely, PSU Bank, Healthcare and Pharma emerged as top gainers.

. National Legal Services Day is being observed across the country today. The day marks the implementation of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, which came into force on this day in 1995 to provide free legal aid to the needy. On this day, legal awareness camps are held by State Legal Services Authorities across the country, regarding the availability of free legal aid and other services provided by the Legal Services Authorities.India is the largest democracy in the world. The Constitution of India guarantees equal rights and the equal protection under the law to every citizen. The day is primarily celebrated to educate people about their legal rights and promote mechanisms for dispute resolution through a number of projects and activities to create a more equitable society.The nationwide network of free legal aid, supported by Lok Adalats, fast-track courts, legal awareness programmes allow for quick and easy dispute resolution. More than 34 crore cases have been disposed of in the last ten years through National Lok Adalats. The day is primarily celebrated to promote legal awareness and ensure access to justice for all citizens, especially those from marginalized communities.

. The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the month-long fifth nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) campaign across the country from the 1st of next month. Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Ministry said that this is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken by the Ministry. Electronics and Information Technology Ministry and UIDAI will provide technical support during this campaign. The Ministry said that the initiative will be adopted with a Whole of Government approach with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country with focus on Face Authentication Technology. The Ministry said that face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used both on Android and Apple devices, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.The Campaign will be conducted in an Utsav mode by offering a bouquet of services such as Health Check-ups and Aadhaar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services to be provided to pensioners based on their requirement.

. Global crude oil prices ended with losses this week amid hopes of possible de-escalation of West Asia conflict following the US midterm elections.Brent crude January futures declined 13.3 per cent to settle at 98 US dollars and 32 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude January futures lost 12.3 per cent to end at 89 US dollars and 59 cents per barrel over the week.

. Indian shuttlers Tushar Suveer and Rakshitha Ramraj clinched the men’s and women’s singles titles, at the Telangana India International Challenge 2026 today.India won three of the five titles. The top-seeded men’s doubles pair of Krishna Prasad Garaga and Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy also claimed victory, defeating compatriots Sai Pratheek K and Ruban Kumar Rethinasabapathi 21-12, 21-18.In the men’s singles final, sixth seed Tushar defeated compatriot Bharat Raghav 15-21, 21-18, 21-19.Top seed Rakshitha also emerged victorious in the women’s singles final, beating ninth seed Rujula Ramu 16-21, 21-15, 21-14.India narrowly missed out on a fourth title when Sathish Kumar Karunakaran and Ashwini Ponnappa lost the mixed doubles final to Russia’s Rodion Alimov and Alina Davletova 19-21, 21-11, 21-13.Japan’s Mei Sudo and Mai Tanabe won the women’s doubles title, defeating Thailand’s Phattharin Aiamvareesrisakul and Sarisa Janpeng 21-11, 21-11.

. International Master Anuj Shrivatri of Madhya Pradesh has won the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship in Philippines to become India’s 100th Grandmaster and the first from his state to achieve the title. Shrivatri secured the title after scoring seven points from his final eight games, following a defeat in the opening round. The achievement was particularly significant as chess enthusiasts in India had been awaiting the country’s 100th Grandmaster, while Madhya Pradesh had been waiting for its first player to earn the prestigious title.All India Chess Federation President Nitin Narang has congratulated Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India’s 100th Grandmaster. He described the achievement as a historic milestone and a proud moment for Indian chess, expressing hope that the country would reach 200 Grandmasters next.

. A drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field in Iraq’s Kurdistan region has triggered an energy emergency, reducing electricity generation across the national grid by approximately 2.8 gigawatts. According to media reports, the attack disrupted gas supplies to power stations serving five major cities, including Erbil, Sulaimaniyah, Duhok, Bazian and Chamchamal. Kurdistan Regional Government’s Electricity Ministry spokesperson Omid Ahmed said emergency measures have been initiated to prevent a complete blackout.Hydroelectric stations at Dokan and Darbandikhan dams are being operated to ensure electricity supply to essential facilities, including hospitals and water stations. Kurdish security forces have confirmed the drone strike. However, no group has claimed responsibility. The extent of damage and possible casualties are yet to be ascertained. The attack coincided with security talks between Kurdish authorities and an Iranian delegation, focusing on regional stability and cross-border security cooperation.

. In men’s cricket, India suffered a three-wicket defeat to Pakistan in their Group A clash of the ACC Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman this evening.Batting first, India were bowled out for 208, powered by Arjun Rajput’s 107 off 85 balls. For Pakistan, Rizwanullah, Ali Raza, and Niqab Shafiq each picked up three wickets.In reply, Pakistan chased down the target, losing seven wickets in 48.1 overs, with the help of Hamza Zahoor’s unbeaten 100 off 108 balls. For India, Manal Chauhan took three wickets, while Mohit Ulva scalped two.Earlier, India had won the toss and elected to bat first.

. The government today launched the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards to recognise outstanding startups across the country. The awards recognise not just commercial success but also social impact, sustainability, and scalability. Launching the awards in New Delhi today, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh said that startups can apply under 20 sectoral categories. He said that in addition, there are three special categories for women, students, and the North Eastern region. He added that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade is at the forefront of driving reforms to promote startups. Mr Singh also emphasised the need for more private initiative to bring more startups in the country. He expressed hope that the awards would further boost the startup ecosystem in the country. The Secretary highlighted that the award covers a wide range of domains including agriculture, fintech, aerospace, health, education, and accessibility, among others. The applications for the award will remain open until 20 November this year.In line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of a five-trillion-dollar economy, Startup India supports startups through initiatives such as startup recognition, tax exemptions, regulatory ease, funding access, and capacity building. Launched in 2016, Startup India has transformed India’s entrepreneurial landscape, fostering innovation and empowering youth, women, students, and first-time founders, particularly from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Over two lakh 25 thousand startups have been recognised by DPIIT so far.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have turned net buyers of Indian equities during the first week of November. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have invested 38,971 crore rupees in the domestic stock market, marking a reversal in investment flows. Of the total investment, 38 thousand 519 crore rupees came through purchases on stock exchanges, while 452 crore rupees were invested through the primary market.The shift in FPI’s sentiment was due to sharp sell-off in global technology stocks, triggered by concerns over artificial intelligence-related investments and a possible slowdown in data centre spending. The recent correction in global AI stocks has made Indian equities more attractive to overseas investors.Meanwhile, the debt market witnessed net inflows of 4,319 crore rupees in November so far.

. Bringing festive cheer to Dalal Street, both the National Stock Exchange and the Bombay Stock Exchange will host the special Diwali Muhurat Trading session tomorrow. According to the circular released by the exchanges, the markets will open at 2:20 PM and close at 3:30 PM.The one-hour session also marks the beginning of new Hindu financial year, Vikram Samvat 2083, which starts on Diwali.On this auspicious occasion, the investors make their symbolic trades for prosperity and good fortune in the year ahead. All trades executed during this session will carry normal settlement obligations.

. Indian pacer Mohammed Shami has announced his retirement from Test cricket, bringing the curtain down on his 13-year career in the longest format of the game. However, he will continue to represent India in limited-overs cricket. Shami announced his decision in a social media post. He finished his Test career with 229 wickets from 64 matches at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls.The 36-year-old fast bowler ended his career as India’s sixth-highest wicket-taking fast bowler in Test cricket, behind Kapil Dev, Zaheer Khan, Ishant Sharma, Javagal Srinath and Jasprit Bumrah. With this announcement, Shami brings an end to a significant chapter in his international career while keeping his focus on the shorter formats of the game.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. US President Donald Trump has said renewed military strikes on Iran are highly unlikely if ongoing negotiations make progress. In an interview, Mr. Trump said Washington was seeking a strong agreement on Iran’s nuclear programme and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. However, he did not rule out further military action. Meanwhile, Iran’s Army has claimed that an oil tanker caught fire after hitting naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz.Tehran warned that the strategic waterway would remain closed until all threats were removed. On the other hand, US Central Command said American forces had intercepted a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman for allegedly violating its naval blockade against Iran.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) capped trade margins on MRP of 137 anti-cancer drugs, based on the recommendations of Expert Committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) under Ministry of Health & Family Welfare. The revised prices of these drugs come into effect from today. As on date, 76 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRP for 1225 anti-cancer formulations, covering 121 drugs.Reduction in the MRP have been reported in 1031 formulations of anti-cancer medicines, with 600 brands reporting above 50% reduction and the highest reduction being 96.45%. Further, out of the 137 identified anti-cancer drugs, there are 10-15 drugs which are yet to be launched in India. However, Trade Margin Rationalization (TMR) will be applicable on these drugs also as and when they are launched.  As a result of the price reductions to be effected from today, the estimated annual savings to consumers would be ₹3,502.31 crore.TMR of non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines is an important step taken by the Government in its continued efforts to improve affordability and accessibility of essential anti-cancer medicines for cancer care.

. President Droupadi Murmu has extended her wishes to the people of Uttarakhand on the occasion of the state’s Foundation Day. In a social media post, she said that Uttarakhand has a distinctive identity for its rich cultural heritage, spiritual traditions and unparalleled natural beauty. She highlighted that the people of the state have always made significant contributions to national service, valour and environmental conservation.President Murmu expressed hope that the people of Uttarakhand will continue to strike a balance between environmental protection and sustainable development while taking the state forward on the path of progress.

. Thailand’s Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has inaugurated the Amazing Thailand Grand Diwali Festival 2026 in Bangkok. The 27-day celebration, described as the longest Diwali festival outside India, will continue throughout November across Thailand. The inauguration ceremony was attended by India’s Ambassador to Thailand Puneet Agrawal and senior Thai officials. The event featured a presentation of the Indian classical dance form Kuchipudi by an Indian cultural troupe.The festival is being organised in collaboration with the Indian Embassy, Thailand’s Tourism Authority, Bangkok Metropolitan Administration and Indian diaspora associations. Meanwhile, Diwali was also celebrated with enthusiasm in San Antonio, United States, featuring a colourful river parade, cultural performances, music and Indian cuisine. The celebrations highlighted India’s growing cultural ties with Thailand and the United States.

. In ODI men’s cricket, India defeated New Zealand by four runs under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method following a rain stoppage at the Hnry Stadium in Wellington today. India were 113 for seven in 26 overs, and needed 22 runs from 66 balls when play was called off.Batting first, New Zealand were bowled out for 134 following a disastrous outing in rainy Wellington. India won the first ODI of the five-match series by five wickets, and now leads the rubber 2-nil.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, 50 crore Indians have escaped extreme poverty over the past 12 years. Addressing the jawans on the occasion of Diwali in Bastar, Chhattisgarh yesterday, Prime Minister compared India’s welfare architecture over the past 12 years to a Diwali Rangoli where small, distinct lines come together to form a grand picture.The Prime Minister detailed how Jan Dhan banking, PM Awas pucca homes, collateral-free Mudra loans, SVANidhi support for street vendors, Ayushman Bharat healthcare, free monthly rations, child education policies, Swachh Bharat, and Har Ghar Jal collectively ensured free medicine, free education, and a free kitchen while removing basic anxieties so families once trapped in generational poverty now inherit a stronger future. Prime Minister Modi said, the poor families whose entire lives used to be spent only in worry have now received the assurance of the government, and a new self-confidence has come into them.Pointing out that this victory over poverty is deeply linked to the fight against Naxalism, which previously trapped lakhs of innocent citizens in deprivation by blocking schools, hospitals, medical stores, polio vaccinations, mobile towers, and industries while bombing railway tracks, the Prime Minister detailed the special development drive in Left-Wing Extremism-affected areas that built over 15,000 kilometres of roads, over 9,500 mobile towers, nearly 175 Eklavya schools, around 50 ITIs, 50 Skill Development Centres, and thousands of post offices, bank branches, and ATMs, alongside rehabilitating surrendered Naxals and bringing water, electricity, and roads to remote tribal villages for the first time under PM JANMAN.Stating that the ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ campaign energized the fight against poverty and brought an end to Naxal violence alongside lifting 50 crore people out of extreme poverty, the Prime Minister cited the ongoing Bastar Olympics as a symbol of transformation in the region. Today in this very Bastar, the Bastar Olympics are taking place, and children are trying their hand at sports, not guns, remarked Shri Modi.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal and Andaman and Nicobar Islands till tomorrow. IMD said that Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep will experience thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds during the same period. The Met Department has said that Eastern parts of the country will experience gradual fall in maximum temperature by two to three degree Celsius over the next three days.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast partly cloudy sky and moderate fog at most places in Delhi tomorrow morning. Further, the air quality in Delhi-NCR continues to remain in the very poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 360 as of 1 PM. An Air Quality Index between 0 and 50 is considered good, 51 and 100 satisfactory, 101 and 200 moderate, 201 and 300 poor, and 301 and 400 very poor. An AQI between 401 and 500 is considered severe.

. In Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir, the Joint Awami Action Committee has demanded an immediate halt to firing and the use of force against civilians by Pakistani security forces. The demand follows reports of several deaths, including women and children, and dozens of injuries during firing and drone attacks on peaceful protesters in the Rawalakot region.The JAAC has called for the immediate return of bodies to bereaved families, proper medical treatment for the injured and restoration of mobile and internet services. It has also demanded an independent, impartial and time-bound investigation into the killings, injuries and arrests. Meanwhile, the United Kashmir People’s National Party has condemned the attacks on protesters and residential areas. The organisation has urged the United Nations to constitute an independent international fact-finding mission to investigate human rights violations in PoJK.

. Wall Street ended on a mixed note yesterday. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.1 per cent as investors returned to AI-related and chip stocks after the recent sell-off, while the S&P 500 gained 0.3 per cent. Conversely, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell half a per cent.All three major indices posted losses for the week. The Nasdaq lost 3.4 per cent, the S&P 500 dropped 2.7 per cent and the Dow slipped 0.9 per cent.On the economic front, the US labour market strengthened in October. Nonfarm payrolls rose by 1 lakh 65 thousand, while the unemployment rate fell marginally to 4.1 per cent from 4.2 per cent in September, according to the data released by the US Bureau of Labour Statistics.

. In tennis, India’s Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale finished runners-up in the women’s doubles at the WTA 250 Chennai Open today. The Indian pair lost 2-6, 0-6 to Switzerland’s Simona Waltert and Naima Karamoko in the final.Despite the defeat in the title clash, Adkar and Bhosale made history by becoming the first all-Indian pair to reach a WTA Tour-level doubles final.Yesterday in the semifinals, the Indian duo defeated second seeds Weronika Falkowska and Alana Smith 6-2, 2-6, [10-8] to move into the final.

Representatives from nearly 200 countries are gathering on Turkey’s Mediterranean coast from today for a two-week United Nations climate conference, COP31, amid mounting global energy and environmental challenges. The talks are expected to focus on accelerating electrification, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting renewable energy. However, the ongoing Iran conflict, rising dependence on coal and increasing electricity demand from artificial intelligence have complicated climate efforts.The United States is also staying away from international climate cooperation for the second consecutive year. Climate-vulnerable nations are demanding a clear roadmap to phase out fossil fuels, while oil-producing countries favour continued use with emission-control technologies. The United Nations has warned that the world is on course to exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius warming limit.

. American multinational technology company, Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The company’s board of directors made the announcement  after Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive Alice Huanga, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, whom US intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing. Huang apologised in a message to the company, saying he was unfaithful to his wife and his actions hurt her and their children for which he is deeply sorry.Nvidia’s board said in a statement it has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, the board said.Last month, US intelligence agencies had discovered that Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended his greetings to the people of Uttarakhand on the occasion of the its Foundation Day. In a social media post, the Prime Minister described Uttarakhand as a divine land rich in spiritual consciousness and breathtaking natural beauty. He noted that the state, with its picturesque mountain landscapes, sacred rivers and the holy Char Dham, also has a distinct identity rooted in its cultural heritage.Mr Modi said that Uttarakhand is scaling new heights of development in every field, with the active participation of its hardworking, talented and progressive people. He expressed confidence that the state, cherished for its natural beauty and rich culture, will continue to advance rapidly on the path of progress. The Prime Minister also prayed that the special occasion will bring happiness, peace and prosperity to people of Uttarakhand.

Seven passengers were killed and 112 others injured yesterday after one train ran into the back of another in Egypt’s Giza Governorate, near Cairo, throwing several passenger carriages off the tracks. The crash happened near El-Ayyat, on the line that carries Cairo-Aswan services, with the Health Ministry describing the first casualty count as preliminary.Seventy-two ambulances rushed to the scene to carry the wounded to hospitals. Of the injured, 49 were taken to El-Wasta Hospital, 29 to El-Ayyat Hospital and 10 to Atfih Hospital. Four bodies were initially recovered, two of them at El-Wasta Hospital, one at Atfih Hospital and one at the site.Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar directed all hospitals in Giza and Beni Suef to be on high alert and ensure that the injured received every form of emergency and medical care. In a social media post, the Health Ministry said, Health Minister monitors emergency and medical services following the El-Ayyat train accident in Giza Governorate.President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ordered an investigation into the crash and said anyone found negligent would be held to account. Sisi, reacting on social media, said he was following the aftermath with great concern.<>

. In the bullion market, gold and silver prices rebounded last week. The rise was supported by steep decline in crude oil prices over hopes of policy shifts following the US midterm elections. Meanwhile, concerns surrounding the global artificial intelligence sector also drove sharp flows from equity markets to commodity markets.At the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), Gold futures for December contract gained nearly 2.7 percent to settle at 1 lakh 42 thousand 167 rupees per 10 grams during the week. Silver futures for December contract rose almost 3.2 percent to close at 1 lakh 84 thousand 787 rupees per kilogram.Meanwhile, at the Commodity Exchange (COMEX), Gold futures for the December contract jumped 4.5 percent during the week to settle at 4,074.9 dollars per troy ounce. Silver futures for the December contract climbed 5.4 percent over the week to end at 51.94 dollars per troy ounce.

Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators are set to hold two-day talks in Abu Dhabi from tomorrow, marking their first meeting since February, with the aim of ending the nearly five-year-long conflict in Ukraine. Security guarantees are expected to dominate the discussions, amid continuing hostilities and intensified missile and drone attacks by both sides.Russia is demanding territorial concessions from Ukraine and an end to its NATO membership demand. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has rejected these conditions, insisting on a ceasefire and firm security guarantees against future aggression. The United States is seeking practical arrangements to address the security concerns of all parties. Meanwhile, European participation remains contentious, with Moscow opposing their involvement at this stage.

. Indian Railways has announced 1,265 vacancies for Station Master posts across various Railway Recruitment Boards and zones, opening up new employment opportunities for graduate candidates. The Railways Ministry said that in an important recruitment-related decision, the Railway Board has prescribed that Station Master recruitment will be notified separately from 2026 onwards. The dedicated recruitment process provides candidates with a specific notification covering eligibility requirements, examination procedures and vacancy distribution for the post. The online application window will remain open till 25th of next month. Candidates are advised to review the detailed eligibility conditions, vacancy distribution and application instructions before submitting their forms. The recruitment reflects Indian Railways’ continued efforts to provide career opportunities to eligible candidates while strengthening its operational workforce.

Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today highlighted that India’s civilizational consciousness will offer valuable guidance in dealing with present day challenges in the country. The Minister stated this at the book launch of Timeless India: Protection and Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the leadership of the Prime Minister in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat said that this book offers a unique perspective on the initiatives undertaken by the government to safeguard and revive India’s rich cultural heritage. He emphasised that preserving and revitalising this legacy is essential not only for safeguarding the country’s historical identity but also for shaping its future.This book is written by Former Rajya Sabha Member Tarun Vijay and  published by Indira Gandhi National Centre of Arts and Surbhi publication.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

French Foreign ​Minister Jean-Noel Barrot has said  that European officials will participate in talks on Ukraine in Abu Dhabi this week.  France will be in Abu Dhabi ​to take part in these discussions, Barrot said.Earlier, US envoy Steve Witkoff had said that Washington would bring delegations from Ukraine and Russia together in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 to discuss ending Moscow’s war against Ukraine, post-war security agreements and de-escalation.US President Donald Trump on Thursday told reporters that the war was close to being settled and that ending it might involve all of Europe. US Secretary of State ​Marco Rubio said Trump was likely alluding to progress on security guarantees ​for Ukraine and Europe. Trump envoy Jared Kushner said US officials meeting in Brussels ⁠on Thursday ​held productive and substantive discussions with Ukraine, NATO ​and European partners on security guarantees for Ukraine and a broader European security architecture.

. Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

Bringing festive cheer to Dalal Street, both the National Stock Exchange and the Bombay Stock Exchange will host the special Diwali Muhurat Trading session today.According to the circulars released by the exchanges, the markets will open at 2:20 PM and close at 3:30 PM. The one-hour session also marks the beginning of the new Hindu financial year, Vikram Samvat 2083, and coincides with Diwali celebrations. All trades executed during this session will carry normal settlement obligations.

. Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan has greeted the people of Uttarakhand on its Foundation Day today. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan wished that Uttarakhand continue to progress and prosper, scaling new heights of development while preserving its rich cultural heritage and natural beauty.

The Election Commission today directed Chief Electoral Officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland to provide one more opportunity to voters who were left out during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR).In a statement, the Commission said that voters who were issued enumeration forms but whose names could not be included in the draft electoral roll on account of being marked as Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate will be provided one more opportunity to get their names included in the final electoral roll.The Commission has directed Chief Electoral Officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland to display the lists of such electors afresh and facilitate the submission of their Enumeration Forms. The booth-level officers have also been asked to contact the electors and assist them with the process, including online submission through the ECINET platform. Special provisions have also been made for electors who have shifted residence within the state and homeless persons.The Commission has also asked to establish a monitoring mechanism to ensure that no eligible elector is deprived of the opportunity in the Final Electoral Roll while preventing duplicate enrolments.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his 139th ‘Mann Ki Baat’ programme has paid his respects to the ‘Father of Fiber Optics’ – Padma Vibhushan Dr. Narinder Singh Kapany on his birth centenary on October 31st. The PM has asked the youth to draw inspiration from such great scientists.Dr Kapany worked at an ordnance factory in India where he learned to make optical instruments. Later, while working with Professor Harold Hopkins at the Imperial College London in the early1950s he demonstrated that images could be transmitted through bundles of flexible glass fibers. After receiving his Ph.D. in optics, he coined the term “fiber optics” in an article in Scientific American.Akashvani Punjab Correspondent reports that “Born on October 31, 1926, in Moga, Punjab, to Sardar Sundar Singh and Smt. Kundan Kaur, Dr. Kapany grew up in Dehradun and graduated from Agra University. Besides being known as a world class renowned scientist, he was also a philanthropist. His daughter, Ms. Kiran Kaur Kapany, who is settled in America, told Akashvani that no story of Dr. Kapany is complete without his wife, Satinder Kaur. Her steadfast encouragement gave him the resilience to keep going as he pioneered new technology.Together with his wife, Dr. Kapany also co-founded the Sikh Foundation, a charitable organization and built one of the finest collections of Sikh art. Guru Nanak Dev University, Amritsar, had the honour to present Dr. Kapany with an honoris causa before his death in the year 2020 and celebrated his birth centenary as well. GNDU Vice Chancellor , Dr Karamjit Singh while speaking about Dr. Kapany’s contribution said.“In his last years, Dr Kapany wrote his memoir, “The Man Who Bent Light.” He passed away peacefully in California on December 3rd, 2020.

In Tennis, India’s Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale will aim to create history when they take on Switzerland’s Naima Karamoko and Simona Waltert in the women’s doubles final of the WTA tournament at SDAT Tennis Stadium, Chennai, this evening.The Indian pair will become the first all-Indian team to contest a WTA Tour-level doubles final, with the title clash scheduled to begin at 4 p.m. IST. Adkar and Bhosale booked their place in the final after defeating second seeds Weronika Falkowska and Alana Smith 6-2, 2-6, [10-8] in a thrilling semifinal yesterday.A victory would mark a significant milestone for Indian women’s tennis, as Adkar and Bhosale look to cap their memorable campaign with a historic WTA doubles crown.
